assessment.nobel_worthiness: Sequencing-by-synthesis with reversible terminators and clonal clusters turned DNA reading into a massively parallel chemical and optical measurement, and it changed what researchers and clinicians can do: population genomics, cancer diagnostics, noninvasive prenatal testing and pathogen surveillance. The enabling steps are chemical (reversible terminators, fluorophore design, surface chemistry), which gives it a clear home in chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman conceived and built the Solexa chemistry and single-molecule approach, and this is the most defensible two-person core. Rothberg (pyrosequencing, ion semiconductor), Mayer (colony sequencing) and Ju (terminator chemistry) also contributed, so the credit is crowded and a two-person prize would exclude several parallel contributors.
assessment.maturity: Two decades of routine, independently reproduced use at enormous scale; recognition is clearly timely or overdue. The impact is among the most validated of any candidate.
uncertainties: Priority and credit among competing massively parallel platforms is contested, and I am relying on my own recollection of that history rather than verified facts.
Some may view sequencing as biology or technology rather than chemistry.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles solved the delivery problem for nucleic-acid drugs and made siRNA therapeutics (patisiran) and mRNA vaccines practical. As a bioengineer I see this as a molecular-design principle (pKa-tuned lipids that are neutral in circulation and charged in the endosome) with immediate, large clinical consequences.
assessment.attribution: Cullis and colleagues developed ionizable-lipid LNP formulation and its scalable manufacture; Anderson and Langer developed lipidoid and combinatorial lipid libraries. MacLachlan, Hope and Madden made decisive contributions that a three-person cap would leave out, so the allocation is genuinely difficult.
assessment.maturity: Validated by approved siRNA drugs and by billions of mRNA vaccine doses; the interpretation is stable. The related mRNA nucleoside-modification work was recognized in 2023, so timing is plausible but the credit split is unresolved.
uncertainties: Which of the several groups and companies should be credited is disputed and I cannot resolve it.
Overlap with the 2023 Medicine prize may weigh against it in the committee's judgment.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors convert a base pair chemically (cytidine or adenosine deamination on a Cas-bound strand) without double-strand breaks, an elegant protein-chemistry design that makes precise point-mutation correction possible. It is spreading rapidly into therapeutics and tools for biology.
assessment.attribution: Liu's laboratory conceived and developed both cytosine and adenine base editors, with Komor and Gaudelli as lead trainees. Liu alone is a clean and credible attribution, though Komor and Gaudelli are credited names and some may argue for them. Doudna and Charpentier were recognized in 2020 for CRISPR, so this is a distinct step.
assessment.maturity: Independent replication is broad and the first clinical use in patients has been reported, but long-term clinical outcomes are still accumulating. Recognition would be somewhat early but defensible.
uncertainties: Therapeutic benefit is only beginning to be demonstrated, so the clinical record is short.
Possible perception that it is a follow-on to the 2020 CRISPR prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetic code expansion with orthogonal tRNA/synthetase pairs lets cells incorporate designed noncanonical amino acids at chosen sites. It gives molecular-level control over protein chemistry, with uses in photocrosslinking, bioorthogonal labeling, biotherapeutics and cell biology, and is widely used as a tool.
assessment.attribution: Schultz and Wang established the first eukaryotic and bacterial orthogonal pairs, Chin extended the approach to eukaryotic cells, multicellular organisms and quadruple codons, and Mehl and Yokoyama also made important contributions. The three named seem the most natural core, though Mehl and Yokoyama make the choice less clear.
assessment.maturity: More than twenty years of independent work and broad adoption in research, with growing industrial application (site-specific antibody-drug conjugates). The recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Contributions of Mehl and Yokoyama may be judged decisive by others.
Whether the field has delivered transformative therapeutic products yet is not something I have verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reading single DNA and RNA molecules by electrical current through a nanopore is a molecular sensor concept: biological pores (alpha-hemolysin, MspA) engineered for single-molecule recognition. Portable nanopore sequencers have made real-time sequencing possible in the field and in clinics, and the sensing principle extends to proteins and small molecules.
assessment.attribution: Deamer, Branton, Kasianowicz and Church conceived the idea; Bayley engineered the pore and demonstrated single-molecule stochastic sensing; Akeson demonstrated strand-processive translocation with an enzyme motor. Branton has died. The three named are my proposal, but the credit allocation among Kasianowicz, Deamer and Branton is an open question.
assessment.maturity: Mature as a commercial technology with extensive independent validation, although accuracy for some applications has taken time to reach competitive levels, and protein sequencing remains unproven.
uncertainties: The priority of the original concept among Deamer, Branton and Kasianowicz is disputed.
Whether the prize would bundle the pore engineering and the enzyme-motor sequencing into one discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Shokat's covalent targeting of the mutant KRAS G12C cysteine, through tethering and a switch-II pocket, opened a protein long considered undruggable, and led to approved drugs. His chemical genetics of analog-sensitive kinases is a general tool for dissecting signaling. This is a clear case of a chemical idea changing clinical oncology.
assessment.attribution: Shokat is the clear leading figure for both the KRAS and the chemical genetics parts, so a single-laureate attribution is clean. Other groups and companies (Amgen, Mirati, Wellspring) developed the clinical molecules, and I treat those as development rather than discovery.
assessment.maturity: Clinical drugs have been approved and the interpretation is stable, but long-term efficacy is limited by resistance, so there is a question whether recognition is premature.
uncertainties: The compound nature (KRAS covalent drugging versus analog-sensitive kinases) may need a different framing.
Resistance and modest durability in patients may temper enthusiasm.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: PROTACs and molecular glue degraders create a new modality, using small molecules to harness the ubiquitin-proteasome system and remove a protein rather than inhibit it. This is a clean molecular-design principle that is spreading across pharmaceuticals and chemical biology.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies conceived and demonstrated the PROTAC concept, and Handa identified cereblon as the thalidomide target, linking molecular glues to the mechanism. Ciulli, Gray and others made major later contributions, so the three-person limit is an uncomfortable fit.
assessment.maturity: Many compounds are in clinical trials, but no PROTAC drug has yet been approved to my knowledge, so clinical validation is incomplete and recognition may be early.
uncertainties: Absence of an approved PROTAC drug (to my knowledge; not verified) makes timing uncertain.
Thalidomide-related mechanism may be seen as a medicine or pharmacology matter.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Activity-based protein profiling uses reactive probes to report on enzyme function in complex proteomes rather than abundance, enabling inhibitor discovery and imaging of enzyme activity. The tool is widely used across chemical biology and drug discovery.
assessment.attribution: Cravatt is the main figure, and the credited names include Bogyo, Weerapana and Overkleeft. Bogyo is a plausible second laureate (probes for imaging and cysteine proteases), but the picture of who made the decisive contribution is not entirely clear to me.
assessment.maturity: Well established for about two decades with many independent users and clinical-stage compounds discovered through it. Recognition would be timely, though less visibly transformative than other candidates.
uncertainties: Whether the discovery is seen as a platform tool or a conceptual breakthrough.
Early work by Cravatt and Bogyo is attributed alongside Overkleeft and others, so priority is not settled.
